title: An old record by Arthur Frye's band and the Vanguard 78s
summary: Dickenson will find a record of a military bandleader and shows his original Vanguard 78s, including Sleepy Time.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I've got a -- I've got a big thick record here that a guy gave me up in Boston. Arthur Frye (PHONETIC) singing -- Arthur Frye (PHONETIC).
Yeah, he was a -- he had a military band or something like that.
He had a band.
Yeah, like Sousa. Somebody like that.
Yeah. I don't remember what I did with that record now. (Inaudible). I'll go get it and show it to you. I know practically where it's at.
Is that your collector's items?
Oh this is small records here you know. The Vanguards.
Oh the Vanguards. Those are nice.
Here's two of them. I ain't got the other two -- I wish I could find them.
You mean the original ones?
Huh?
I have --
Yeah, these are some of the originals.
Yeah, I have a 10 inch one. They have been reissued since.
Yeah, but there was four of these (inaudible).
Yeah, yeah. In fact they -- I think they just recently came out in England again. Yeah, I have that one too.
You got this one?
Yeah, the -- they're singing that aren't they -- "Sleepy Time."
Yeah, "Sleepy Time." These things ain't much protection you know.
Yeah. Was it in there that Frye was --
No, it's in that -- in -- it's in that -- it's in my other record case. I keep these out of the
way -- the wax records you know. Most of them.
Oh they're 78s. I got a lot of those still.
(End of proceedings as recorded)
